ideas.risks: Could fail if fixed-slack oracle only gives additive guarantee with respect to target class and cannot be made robust under adversarial relabeling; proof may require assumptions like realizability on trimmed distributions that are not distribution-free.
ideas.summary: Develop a polynomial-time **distribution-free residual-forcing wrapper**: repeatedly call the fixed-slack learner on weighted restrictions of the sample where points with high disagreement under current consensus are re-weighted/dropped, creating a sequence of filters so that each stage either certifies low OPT or forces a noticeable gain in one-step correlation, with total variation of weights controlled to keep sample complexity polynomial in 1/epsilon.
ideas.title: Residual-forcing wrapper with controlled rejection sampling
ideas.why_promising: Could avoid the typical combinatorial clean-subset enumeration by maintaining weights explicitly; similar to multiplicative-weights style distillation may preserve weak-edge guarantees while converting constant residual to arbitrary epsilon when combined with martingale-style stopping.

ideas.risks: May collapse on computational hardness because each boosting step may need solving NP-hard weighted empirical risk minimization over C or its hypotheses; also statistical soundness may require stronger access than IID samples.
ideas.summary: Search for a **conditional hardness reduction** from efficient strong agnostic learning to a known hard problem using only a fixed-slack agnostic improper learner as subroutine. Candidate shape: construct distributions where every hypothesis has excess risk either <beta or >1/2-beta-like gap, so fixed-slack suffices for weak signal but epsilon-accuracy would solve hard prediction/refutation tasks.
ideas.title: Hardness collapse via weak-slack oracle flattening
ideas.why_promising: If successful, gives an explicit separation theorem under plausible assumptions and explains why no general positive reduction can exist without new assumptions; fits the run goal of serious negative direction.

ideas.risks: May only prove efficiency for restricted concept families; if subclass conditions are too strong, impact is narrow and may not advance open edge for full class.
ideas.summary: Characterize a **sufficient subclass condition** under which the implication is polynomially true: e.g., classes with efficiently estimable empirical Rademacher complexity bounds and stable closure under self-labeling, where residual errors can be converted to confidence-weighted majorities with explicit variance control.
ideas.title: Identify maximal subclass where fixed-slack implies full agnostic
ideas.why_promising: Even a strong conditional theorem (e.g., finite-VC + efficient calibration oracle + low-noise margin stability) gives a nontrivial positive branch and can guide where obstruction likely lies in the general case.

ideas.risks: Could be too loose: known lower bounds may already rule out sublinear dependence on some model parameter; constructing a hard family may accidentally rely on unproven cryptographic assumptions too weak to be accepted.
ideas.summary: Try **distribution-dependent counterexample families with high-probability label randomization** where any strong learner needs identifying a hidden secret, but fixed-slack learner can always output coarse majority-based hypotheses exploiting the constant gap. Formalize as gap-heavy mixtures where OPT can be made arbitrarily small yet noise-tail structure thwarts boosting.
ideas.title: Gap-mixture counterexample family with planted secrets
ideas.why_promising: Targets the exact weak-vs-strong divide; if a family with efficient weak-improper learner and hard strong-improper can be built, it settles the edge negatively or conditionally.

ideas.risks: Hard to prove cleanly that each step gains independent additive reduction in excess; existing analysis may hide hidden dependence on class size or failure probability that becomes exponential.
ideas.summary: Revisit known agnostic boosting algorithms (e.g., residual-free variants) and isolate the exact complexity blowups to see if they can be replaced by **online-to-batch/median-of-means amplification**. The goal is a fully explicit runtime proof that stays poly in VC(C), log|H|, d, and 1/epsilon with fixed beta oracle calls treated as unit-cost statistical subroutine.
ideas.title: Tight complexity audit of existing agnostic boosters
ideas.why_promising: The existing blockage is explicitly 'efficiency accounting'; a line-by-line audit may reveal a previously overlooked route to polynomial dependence that is not a brand-new theorem.

ideas.risks: SQ framework may not faithfully capture improper-output constraints or distributional requirements in this atlas definition; reductions can lose constants and fail to transport back to PAC format.
ideas.summary: Model the fixed-slack learner as an SQ oracle with unknown tolerance induced by beta, then prove or refute whether any efficient agnostic learner can be simulated with polynomial tolerance schedule. Search for an **agnostic-SQ barrier**: need >poly precision to remove slack, impossible under standard polynomial-query bounds.
ideas.title: SQ perspective on fixed-slack-to-arbitrary-epsilon gap
ideas.why_promising: SQ lower bounds are standard for separating weak/strong tasks; this route gives crisp formal obstructions and may convert loose intuition into a conditional theorem.
